headline: High-risk workspace and tool-use overlap from Cline; B is local-only, so leakage and compliance risks are limited but interaction hazards remain.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cline can read workspace files, run browsers, and use MCP, so attacker-controlled content in shared files or MCP outputs could influence it. godot_rl_agents has no input surfaces or outputs documented, so the pairwise bridge is one-way and inferred from Cline’s documented surfaces. This is not provably blocked, but the second agent does not add a direct injection channel.
conditions: IF Cline reads attacker-controlled workspace files or MCP responses as instructions, injection is possible.
IF an orchestrator copies Cline output into another agent’s prompt, the risk increases.
mitigations: Restrict Cline to a clean workspace folder.
Disable or whitelist MCP servers for the session.
Review browser/file outputs before reuse.
Separate any downstream agent prompts from raw Cline text.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cline touches source code and browser screenshots and can write/read the workspace, while godot_rl_agents shows no data classes or I/O surfaces and no network egress. The pair does not document a shared sensitive-data path, so leakage is limited to local workspace exposure rather than outbound exfiltration. The absence of B-side surfaces lowers the blast radius.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace directory, Cline can expose files B can also read locally.
IF Cline is configured to open browser sessions on sensitive pages, screenshots may persist in the workspace.
mitigations: Use separate workspaces for the two agents.
Remove secrets from shared folders.
Turn off browser capture when not needed.
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cline has broad filesystem write, shell, and git modification capabilities with shared state via filesystem across instances. godot_rl_agents has no documented write, network, or concurrency surfaces, so there is no clear write-write conflict with B. The main conflict is Cline-versus-Cline or Cline-versus-orchestrator, not a strong pairwise clash.
conditions: IF both agents are given write access to the same directory, Cline can overwrite files B depends on.
IF the orchestrator maps B to mutable shared state, conflicts become more likely.
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories.
Avoid shared git branches during concurrent runs.
Serialize writes to any common files.
Use read-only mounts for B.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cline can generate code, browser-derived content, and file edits that a downstream agent could treat as authoritative. godot_rl_agents has no documented verification or critique surface, so if its outputs are fed from Cline, the pair can propagate errors without a built-in check. The interaction is inferred, but the default Cline tool loop makes this plausible.
conditions: IF B consumes Cline-generated files or summaries as ground truth, errors can cascade.
IF Cline’s browser output is copied into B without verification, false facts can propagate.
mitigations: Require human review of Cline outputs before reuse.
Add a verification step before B acts on any Cline artifact.
Keep B on independent inputs.
Log source provenance for every shared artifact.
requires-engineering: implement automated consistency checks.

E_compliance.rationale: Cline handles model-provider API keys and browser screenshots, while godot_rl_agents documents no regulated data classes, residency, or retention constraints. With only one agent clearly touching potentially sensitive operational data, the compliance issue is mainly local handling and logging rather than a documented cross-border or PHI breach. The second agent is not cited because it has no compliance-relevant fields.
conditions: IF Cline is used on regulated source code or screenshots containing personal data, retention controls matter.
IF screenshots or logs are stored outside the intended jurisdiction, residency concerns arise.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in the workspace.
Purge screenshots after use.
Limit log retention in the host environment.
Confirm provider terms for any secrets handled.
requires-engineering: add jurisdiction-aware storage controls.
